question:
(i) What is meant by distance of closest approach in Rutherford’s $\alpha$-particle scattering experiment?
(ii) How will this distance change if the kinetic energy of the incident $\alpha$-particle is doubled? Justify your answer.

options.A:
(i) In a head-on approach, the distance of closest approach is the minimum distance from the nucleus at which the alpha particle momentarily stops as its kinetic energy converts to electrostatic potential energy.
(ii) Since $r_0=\dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\dfrac{2Ze^2}{K}$, $r_0\propto\dfrac1K$; doubling kinetic energy makes the distance half.
options.B:
(i) It is the impact parameter of a grazing alpha particle.
(ii) It doubles when kinetic energy is doubled.
options.C:
(i) It is the radius of the alpha particle.
(ii) It does not depend on kinetic energy.
options.D:
(i) It is the minimum distance only for an electron.
(ii) It becomes four times on doubling kinetic energy.
